scope: Theorem 9.1 (Stopping-band transfer) of the manuscript “Buffered comparison and stopping-band resolution in critical Ising” (preprints/Buffered-comparison-and-stopping-band-resolution-in-critical-Ising-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 218 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 d5167e3fe5fb85f4), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF pages 39-40. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. statement: Fix an inward or outward band, target, and ambient square chart as in Section 7, with all the stated positive clearances. Use the critical plus-boundary 39 law in the fixed larger reference square. For every exceptional probability ϵ > 0 and target error η > 0, generic contour levels can be chosen in any prescribed separated subwindows so that the following hold for all sufficiently fine meshes. 1. The stopping observation of Lemma 7.2 has a finite descriptor Zδ ∈ {0, 1, . . . , m}, computed from band spins. State 0 is exceptional and has probability at most ϵ in the fixed reference chart. 2. Every good state i has a deterministic regular signed barrier Γi. For every realizable transcript with Zδ = i, adding its plus pins and then its minus pins changes the target law by a sum of at most η in total variation. The resulting target-side Gibbs law, denoted Qi,δ, is the same for every such transcript. This assertion is uniform over all bounded observables on the target. 3. In the inward case one may also move the full barrier to a slightly farther signed contour, retaining the entire enclosed free component as the kept volume. Counting the two old-pin removals as well, the sum of target errors can still be made at most η. The final kept volume has a positive macroscopic buffer from its fixed boundary. All geometric clearances have positive minima over the good states. 4. For a fixed finite list of bands the descriptors have convergent joint laws. The bins can be chosen to be continuity sets of the limiting data law; hence this finite-space convergence is in total variation. The number of states, their barriers, and their positive clearances depend on the fixed geometry and on ϵ, η, not on the mesh. The threshold for the mesh is chosen afterward. If a different law, possibly conditional on remote pins, has band density at most K times that of the reference chart by Corollary 2.5, its exceptional probability is at most Kϵ. The same applies to mixtures of those conditional laws.
